statement: There is no finite universal C such that Var_mu(f) <= C integral |grad f|^2 dmu for every log-concave probability measure mu on R, without any covariance or scale normalization.
assumptions: mu_s=N(0,s^2), s>0; f(x)=x belongs to W^{1,2}(mu_s).
proof: Var_mu_s(x)=s^2 while integral |f'|^2 dmu_s=1. For each proposed C choose s^2>C.

statement: For every n>=2 an isotropic uniform simplex measure and an edge-parallel unit direction have line-conditionals with essential-supremum Poincare constant 2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2 and mean Poincare constant 12/pi^2, in inherited Euclidean arclength.
assumptions: Full-dimensional centered uniform measure on the whitened standard simplex
Essential supremum uses the projected law
proof_or_counterexample: Whiten using Sigma^{-1}=(n+1)(n+2)(I+J). Fiber length is sqrt(2(n+1)(n+2))*T with T~Beta(2,n-1). Interval C_P=L^2/pi^2; E T^2=6/((n+1)(n+2)); every neighborhood of T=1 has positive probability.

statement: On the C02 simplex, f_k=T^k cos(pi X_1/T), k>=1 integer, is Lipschitz and its conditional-variance/directional-energy quotient equals (2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2)*(2k)(2k+1)/((n+2k-1)(n+2k)). For k>1 this exceeds the mean fiber constant 12/pi^2. Thus pulling the average fiber constant outside a fiber-energy expectation is false.
assumptions: Same simplex, projection and Euclidean direction as C02
Only directional energy is in this quotient, not full gradient energy
proof_or_counterexample: Conditional mean is zero, conditional variance T^(2k)/2, directional energy pi^2*T^(2k-2)/(4a). Beta moments give the quotient; at n=100,k=10 it is 50.5 times the proposed average constant.
